exposure: Maternal conditions (e.g., complications of placenta, cord, and membranes; hypertensive diseases of pregnancy)
Fetal causes (e.g., fetal developmental disorder, extremely low birth weight)
outcome: Stillbirths (early and late fetal deaths, categorized as antepartum and intrapartum)
cohort: The study included 475 stillbirths identified from a total of 74,102 births between 2015 and 2020 at a single center in a middle-income country.
finding: Fetal developmental disorder was the most common cause of antepartum fetal death, while intrapartum deaths were mostly due to extremely low birth weight, and complications of placenta, cord, and membranes were the most common maternal conditions involved.
birth_weight: Extremely low birth weight was identified as the cause for 44.6% of intrapartum deaths among the studied stillbirths.
